newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Caracas metro plans $800 mln expansion.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Caracas metro plans $800 mln expansion.

text.p: Caracas's sleek underground metro is planning a $800 million dollar extension to two lines and is only waiting for government approval before it begins looking for financing, Metro president Ignacio Cumbellas said.

The extensions will "turn the current system into a true network ... public transport is absolutely fundamental to this city, there isn't space for more cars," Cumbellas told the Foreign Press Association.

Cumbellas said the company was in on-going discussions with the government over the investment, as well as raising tariffs so as to reduce the state's subsidy to 30 percent by the year 2000 from the current 50 percent level.

Despite a bumpy record of servicing a metro-related $700 million debt that stems from the late 70s, and is held by a consortium of French banks led by Banque Paribas Cumbellas said: "there's $200 million in the kitty to pay-out (for debt) this year."
Over 300 million passengers travel the well-managed and efficient metro each year, making it one of the most densely used in the world in terms of passengers per kilometer, Cumbellas said.
